title: The Goodhart curve, the Gao fit, and reward ensembles
brief: Compute best-of-n exactly on a discrete space, watch gold reward rise and then fall as the proxy keeps climbing, fit the Gao scaling form, and see mean and min ensembles push the peak out.
hints: Sort the outputs by proxy with np.argsort. The chance that the best of n draws is no better than the i-th sorted output is F_i^n, where F_i is the base mass of that output and everything below it. Subtract the same quantity for the output just below.
np.cumsum(base[order]) gives F in sorted order. Write the probabilities back with policy[order] = ..., so they line up with the original outputs.
Both Gao forms are linear in (a, b). Stack the columns [d, -d**2] or [d, -d * log d] into a matrix and call np.linalg.lstsq.
For tilted_policy, work in logs: log(base) + proxy / beta, subtract the maximum, then exponentiate and normalise.
The peak of d * (a - b * d) is at d = a / (2b). If your fit returns b < 0, check the sign of the second column.
